label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of emotional distress. With 165 respondents in this cluster, the profile points to a meaningful subgroup where extensive screen time coincides with compounded psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily internet/screen use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness despite high digital connectivity (UCLA-8 mean 1.74)
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most pronounced distress indicator (GAD-7 mean 2.17)
Heavy daily screen time (more than 5 hours), potentially displacing in-person social interaction
Co-occurrence of all three distress dimensions, suggesting compounded emotional vulnerability
tone: Strained and quietly overwhelmed — reflective of someone managing persistent emotional distress beneath a high-functioning, digitally connected exterior

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all at the low end of their respective scales, these individuals demonstrate generally positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77 on normalized scale)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen time (1–3 hours)
Demonstrates consistent emotional stability across all three psychological measures

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to manage their emotional well-being without significant clinical distress, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders even in the presence of perceived social isolation.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) well below clinical thresholds
Low anxiety symptom burden (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) well below clinical thresholds
Moderate and controlled digital engagement (1–3 hours daily)
Possible reliance on internal coping strategies or academic/professional engagement that mitigates mood disturbance despite social disconnection
tone: Quietly detached yet emotionally stable; reflective and self-contained rather than distressed
